B13_00: Formation of transient actin-rich membrane folds, driven by branched actin polymerisation pushing the plasma membrane forward, is suppressed. A Rac GTPase-activating protein lowers Rac signalling to the nucleation machinery, an ankyrin-repeat protein limits talin-dependent coupling of adhesions to actin, a WAVE complex component fails to promote ruffling, and Ena/VASP and profilin proteins shape filament elongation and monomer supply, restraining spreading and protrusion.
B13_01: Formation of autophagosomes is held in check so that self-digestion matches demand. Chromatin and transcriptional regulators limit expression of autophagy genes, a PHD-finger protein restrains the Beclin-1 initiation complex, kinesin-adaptor proteins interfere with early assembly, and SNARE and Sec1/Munc18 trafficking components govern how much membrane lipid and cargo reach the growing phagophore, forming the negative arm of autophagy initiation.
B13_02: The number and rate of inhibitory synapses formed are controlled at the contact between a presynaptic terminal and its partner, biasing nascent contacts toward an inhibitory identity. Transmembrane and secreted organizers bridge the cleft and recruit postsynaptic scaffolds, clustering gephyrin and GABA-A receptors, while calsyntenin and cerebellin ligands engage presynaptic adhesion partners and semaphorin-plexin signalling tunes contact formation.
B13_03: Centriole duplication is restricted to one new centriole per existing centriole per cycle, keeping centrosome number at two. Ubiquitin ligases restrain amplification and degrade pericentriolar assembly factors, a pericentriolar organiser couples centrosome integrity to mitotic fidelity, other proteins block inappropriate centriole elongation or de novo cartwheel assembly, and acetyltransferases limit duplication licensing, preventing multipolar spindles and chromosome missegregation.
B13_04: Synaptic vesicles are converted into a primed, fusion-competent state, setting the size of the readily releasable pool. Plasma membrane syntaxins provide the target SNARE, a Sec1/Munc18 protein chaperones syntaxin, a Munc13 isoform catalyses transition to the primed state, and tomosyn restrains priming by forming non-fusogenic complexes. NSF-associated SNAP proteins recycle SNAREs, vesicle membrane proteins shape the vesicle, and a kinase adds phosphorylation control.
B13_05: A synapse is assembled precisely at the contact between a nerve terminal and its target cell. A secreted proteoglycan from the nerve activates a receptor tyrosine kinase that clusters acetylcholine receptors beneath the terminal, while a collagen-tailed subunit anchors acetylcholinesterase in the cleft so transmitter is cleared. Six-family transcription factors, scaffolds and ubiquitin ligases tune synaptic protein localisation and terminal growth.
B13_06: Tight junction assembly is held back or reversed, opening the paracellular space and lowering barrier resistance. TNF signalling through the IKK-NF-kB arm disassembles junctional complexes, Rho-associated kinases drive actomyosin contraction that pulls on junction anchors and prevents their maturation, and microRNAs repress junction proteins post-transcriptionally, together reducing epithelial and endothelial sealing and cell polarity.
B13_07: The pointed (minus) end of actin filaments is capped to block subunit addition or loss there, fixing filament length. Tropomodulins bind the pointed end together with tropomyosin, while related leiomodins instead nucleate new filaments and can compete for the same site. The balance between capping and nucleation sets and stabilises uniform filament length in contractile and membrane-associated actin networks.
B13_08: Capping of actin filament barbed ends, where elongation mainly occurs, is regulated to decide whether a network grows or stalls. CARMIL-family proteins bind capping protein and lower its affinity for filament ends, allowing uncapping and renewed growth; myotrophin sequesters or antagonises capping protein; a WASH complex subunit couples capping control to branched nucleation on endosomes; and cofilin severs filaments to create new ends.
B13_09: Assembly of sheet-like branched actin protrusions at the leading edge is restrained, limiting protrusion and letting a cell stop, turn or hold still. Cofilin severs and depolymerises filaments, an Abl-interactor protein dampens WAVE-driven Arp2/3 nucleation, and repulsive cues acting through plexin and Robo receptors collapse protrusions by reducing Rac-dependent polymerisation. An extracellular glycoprotein and microRNAs further suppress the same output.
B13_10: Assembly of the receiving side of a synapse, where receptor scaffolds, actin and adhesion molecules gather, is tuned in speed and extent. Rac GTPases with their DOCK activators and ARHGAP inactivators remodel the actin cytoskeleton, upstream G protein cues feed in, trans-synaptic adhesion and guidance receptors position contacts, and neddylation, retromer trafficking and translational repressors set the local supply of components.
B13_11: Formation of thin finger-like actin bundle protrusions is restrained, limiting their number and emergence rate. A Slit-Robo GAP family protein, partly through a paralogue that antagonises the ancestral form, inhibits Rho-family GTPases and deforms membrane, while small GTPase-dependent membrane traffic, kinase signalling and a presynaptic adhesion molecule add further control, slowing protrusion and the maturation of synaptic contacts.
B13_12: Assembly of the NLRP3 inflammasome, which drives caspase-1 activation, IL-1-family cytokine maturation and pyroptotic death, is restrained. Ubiquitin ligases target the sensor for degradation, macroautophagy and chaperone-mediated autophagy clear it, pyrin-domain-only decoy proteins block adaptor recruitment, and depalmitoylases, kinases and a sirtuin deacetylase tune the sensor through reversible modification, setting the activation threshold.
B13_13: Tubulin polymerization is suppressed and microtubule plus-end extension limited, setting polymer length, enabling dynamic remodelling and freeing tubulin dimers for reuse. Stathmins sequester soluble tubulin dimers and promote catastrophe, a plus-end tracking protein and microtubule-associated proteins and tubulin cofactors tune the resulting polymer, and a dual-specificity kinase and stathmin phosphorylation link the balance to signalling cues.
B13_14: Synapse formation is actively restrained, limiting contact number during circuit refinement. Secreted Wnt ligands and a Dickkopf antagonist suppress synapse formation, Slit ligands with Robo receptors and an Eph receptor deliver repulsive cues that discourage contact, cerebellin and calsyntenin organizers can curb assembly, and Toll-like receptor signalling and an immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion molecule modulate neurite and synapse number.
B13_15: SNARE proteins on two membranes zipper into a four-helix bundle to drive fusion, and this step is promoted or restrained to control where and when fusion occurs. A Sec1/Munc18 protein chaperones syntaxin into a fusion-ready state, other modulators tune pairing, and HOPS and CORVET tethering complexes couple Rab-dependent tethering to SNARE engagement for late endosome and lysosome fusion.
B13_16: Stalled translation initiation complexes and their mRNAs condense into cytoplasmic stress granules, sequestering mRNA from ribosomes. Scaffolding RNA-binding proteins promote condensation, a deubiquitinase acting with G3BP scaffolds restrains it, and AMP-activated protein kinase couples granule dynamics to energy status. Autophagy proteins link granule turnover to degradative clearance, setting how readily granules form and how large they grow.
B13_17: Assembly of proteins into dimers and larger complexes is controlled in occurrence, speed and extent. Acetylation by a coactivator acetyltransferase and deacetylation by a cytoplasmic deacetylase that also routes aggregates to the aggresome, oxygenase-mediated modification, ISG15 conjugation, a tripartite-motif ubiquitin ligase and retromer-dependent endosomal sorting together link post-translational modification, trafficking and quality control to client assembly state.
B13_18: Assembly of a DNA-sensing inflammasome, nucleated by cytosolic double-stranded DNA and committing the cell to caspase-1 activation and pyroptosis, is tuned. Interferon-inducible guanylate-binding proteins lyse pathogen-containing vacuoles to release DNA into the cytosol, a related PYHIN sensor engages DNA, pyrin-domain-only decoys block PYD-PYD polymerisation, and a tripartite-motif ligase adds ubiquitin-dependent control.
B13_19: A bipolar microtubule spindle is assembled for chromosome segregation, with control over its speed and fidelity. ESCRT-III proteins with a VPS4 ATPase and ALIX remodel membranes at the nuclear envelope and midbody, a Polo-like kinase provides master mitotic input, RCC1 generates the chromatin RanGTP gradient releasing spindle assembly factors, and microtubule- and RNA-binding proteins stabilise spindle microtubules and align chromosomes.
